content.value_statement: Designing reliable Claude Code agents is hard without structure. This skill provides templates, validation rules, and examples for agent prompts, triggers, tools, and metadata.
actual_capabilities: Explains the agent markdown format and required YAML frontmatter fields.
Provides trigger description patterns with example user and assistant exchanges.
Guides system prompt structure for autonomous Claude Code agents.
Lists supported model, color, and tool configuration options.
Includes complete agent examples for review, testing, documentation, and security workflows.
Includes a local shell validator for agent file structure checks.
limitations: Focused on Claude Code plugin agents, not general agent frameworks.
Does not install, publish, or run agents automatically.
Validation checks file structure, not real agent behavior quality.
Examples need project-specific review before production use.

use_cases.title: Create Plugin Agents
use_cases.description: Design a new Claude Code plugin agent with frontmatter, trigger examples, and a complete system prompt.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Triggers
use_cases.description: Rewrite vague descriptions into precise triggering rules with examples that help Claude select the right agent.

use_cases.title: Validate Agent Files
use_cases.description: Check that agent markdown files include required fields, valid names, model choices, colors, and prompt content.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner agent creation from a short task description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code agent for this task: [describe task]. Include a clear name, trigger description, model choice, color, tools, and system prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Trigger Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve when an existing agent should activate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent description and make its triggering conditions more precise. Add realistic examples and explain when the agent should not run.

prompt_templates.title: Restrict Agent Tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Apply least privilege to an agent design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this agent purpose and choose the minimum tools it needs. Explain why each tool is necessary and which tools should be excluded.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Agent Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before adding an agent to a plugin.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Claude Code agent for frontmatter quality, trigger clarity, system prompt completeness, tool scope, edge cases, and validation readiness.

output_examples.input: Create an agent for pull request quality reviews.
output_examples.output: A reviewer agent plan with a specific name, clear trigger examples, limited tools, and a structured review prompt.

output_examples.input: Improve a vague agent description for test generation.
output_examples.output: A stronger trigger description that covers new code, missing tests, edge cases, and situations where the agent should stay inactive.

output_examples.input: Check whether an agent file is ready for a plugin.
output_examples.output: A validation summary covering required metadata, naming rules, model and color choices, prompt structure, and recommended fixes.

best_practices: Use precise trigger descriptions with two to four realistic examples.
Restrict agent tools to the minimum needed for the intended workflow.
Test each agent with common requests and edge cases before publishing.
anti_patterns: Using generic agent names or broad descriptions that trigger too often.
Granting full tool access when read-only or narrow tools are enough.
Writing short system prompts without process steps, quality standards, or output expectations.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code plugin agents with frontmatter, trigger examples, tool choices, and system prompts.

faq.question: Does it create agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, templates, examples, and validation steps for you to apply.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata supports Codex, Claude, and Claude Code, but the guidance targets Claude Code agents.

faq.question: Does the validator prove an agent is safe?
faq.answer: No. The validator checks structure and basic content. Human review is still needed for behavior and tool scope.

faq.question: What files should I read first?
faq.answer: Start with the main skill guide, then review the system prompt design reference and complete examples.

faq.question: How should I choose tools for an agent?
faq.answer: Choose the smallest set that supports the task. Prefer read-only tools unless the agent must edit or run commands.
